title: Autopilot Agents: decide the operating model before the rollout
decision: Approve one narrow private-preview pilot only when a named business leader owns the goal, access boundary, cost guardrail, exception path and outcome review.
summary: Bottom line: treat Copilot Autopilot as a bounded standing role, not a better chatbot. Approve one private-preview pilot only where a named leader owns the goal, access boundary, cost and outcomes.

claims.text: Copilot Autopilot, previously called Scout, was announced as a persistent digital teammate with its own identity, memory, computer and workspace; people set its objective and boundaries and remain informed and in control.
Microsoft said Copilot Autopilot was expanding to private preview at the end of September 2026; the announcement does not establish general availability.
As an architectural lens, Microsoft Foundry defines an autopilot by a persistent standing role and its own identity, security profile and accountable manager, not by a changing feature list.
In the Foundry model, autonomy remains bounded: the organization controls when an autopilot responds, who it interacts with, what it accesses and which actions it can take.
The Foundry blueprint model separates reusable agent logic and infrastructure from team-specific business access, with each created instance receiving its own identity, permissions and assignment.

voice.narration:
Bottom line: treat Copilot Autopilot as a bounded standing role, not a better chatbot. Approve one private-preview pilot only where a named leader owns the goal, access boundary, cost and outcomes.

The shift is from asking for an answer to assigning a standing role. Autopilot was announced with identity, memory, a computer and workspace; leaders still set objectives and boundaries. That changes governance, not just productivity.

Foundry provides an architectural lens, not proof that every implementation is identical: identity establishes the role, while capability can change. The organization controls interactions, access and actions, and an accountable manager remains essential.

Pilot one recurring workflow with one team and one accountable owner. Reuse a blueprint for logic, but scope each instance to its own permissions and assignment. Because Copilot Autopilot remains private preview, require a stop condition and outcome review before expansion.
